output.letter:
Razorpay's Senior Software Engineer role on the Payments Platform team aligns closely with my experience owning high-throughput fintech services and driving reliability improvements in production environments. At CRED, I managed the rewards-ledger service processing approximately 3 million ledger entries daily, where I significantly reduced p99 write latency from 380ms to 95ms by implementing batched Kafka consumers and JDBC batch inserts. This experience touches directly on the kind of distributed systems and concurrency challenges central to Razorpay's payments path services.

In my previous role at Razorpay, I built the UPI mandate auto-debit reminders pipeline using Python and AWS serverless technologies, processing around 12 million reminders monthly with a failure rate under 0.1%. Moreover, I enhanced API latency by 38% through denormalizing read-models with Debezium CDC into Redis—experience that speaks to the payment-rails domain familiarity and CDC patterns your JD values. I also authored the team's first chaos-test harness using Toxiproxy, uncovering retry bugs before production deployment, which underscores my commitment to observability and exactly-once messaging patterns.

Beyond engineering, I have mentored junior engineers at CRED and led design pairing sessions, covering essential backend concepts such as caching and idempotency. I have been the primary on-call engineer with a strong track record of leading incident reviews and crafting RCAs, paralleling the responsibilities outlined for this role.

I am eager to bring my backend service ownership and fintech domain expertise to Razorpay's Payments Platform, contributing to robust payment orchestration systems while advancing my skills in Go and Kubernetes-based microservices. I look forward to collaborating on service-level design and enhancing the platform’s observability and resilience.

Best,
Aarav
